- Ran task_switch.sh, committed the task completion as 0afab9c, and pushed master successfully.
- The post-commit hook also rebuilt/published the mdBook and pushed docs repo commit a01d22e5 automatically.
- Remaining worktree changes are unrelated pre-existing source edits outside this task slice; task 02 itself is fully finished and pushed.

- Read .ralph/current_tasks.md and .ralph/current_tasks_done.md to identify active selectable work.
- Confirmed there are no active failing bug tasks in current_tasks, so bug-first does not redirect selection.
- Active failing candidates are five high-priority tasks: general-architecture 08 and ha-acceptance-deletion-first-rewrite 03/04/05/06.
- The HA rewrite tasks form the clearest dependency chain from the already-completed 01 and 02 tasks. Task 04 requires the observation surface after observer removal, and tasks 05/06 explicitly build on the direct observation surface. The earliest unblocked logical next task is story-ha-acceptance-deletion-first-rewrite/03.
- Next step: write that task path into .ralph/current_task.txt and stop immediately.

- Read the progress log and current task pointer.
- Current task is story-ha-acceptance-deletion-first-rewrite/03-task-delete-observer-compose-rendering-and-collapse-ha-fixtures-to-two-static-compose-variants.md.
- Reading the task body now to determine whether this is still TO BE VERIFIED or ready to execute.

- Task is NOW EXECUTE, so I am implementing rather than doing a type-design-only pass.
- Mapped the HA fixture stack: observer service and observer config rendering are threaded through givens/topology/world, but the step layer only needs host-side status, primary routing, switchover requests, and a SQL writable-primary probe.
- Chosen design: remove observer service/types/templates entirely; keep two checked-in compose variants and generate a tiny include-only per-run compose file with `include` long syntax and `project_directory` set to the materialized run dir; move host observation to Rust API-client logic instead of docker exec into an observer container.
- Need to rewrite the observer helper to source auth/TLS from materialized assets, map API/postgres access through published host ports, and update fault isolation to block host->member API access without an observer container.

- All required code/test gates are green now: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long all passed.
- The main fixes beyond the initial rewrite were: API hostname verification via reqwest DNS resolve to host-published ports; reusing the existing observer client cert/key for host-side psql probes; tightening copied private-key permissions to 0600 so libpq accepts them.
- Moving to the required post-test docs pass now, using the k2-docs-loop skill because the task explicitly demands docs updates only after tests pass.
